newsitem.title: USA: General Mills rises on strong earnings.
newsitem.headline: General Mills rises on strong earnings.

text.p: Shares of General Mills Inc rose two to 65-1/4 on Thursday after the company reported better-than-expected earnings for its fiscal second quarter.
"The numbers look better than expected, clearly, from stronger-than-expected cereal volume," said Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez.

General Mills reported net earnings of $1.00 a share for the quarter ended November 24, up from $0.92 a share last year. According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' estimates was $0.95 a share.
The company said its Big G cereals sales volume rose 10 percent, and the cereals hold a 25 percent market share.
"They clearly have momentum in the cereal category right now, driven by new products," said John O'Neil, an analyst for BT Securities.
Sales of new cereals accounted for nearly 2.5 points of the market share, General Mills said. The company said it expects to post record 1997 earnings.
